How It Works

Tournament Format

Schedule
Games every 45 min. Game time is forfeit time. Two 16-min running-clock halves, 2-min halftime.
Guaranteed Games
Every team gets a minimum of 3 games. Top teams advance to Sunday single-elimination bracket for the FITS Championship.
Beach Rules
International Flag guidelines with beach modifications. No shoes or cleats. Flags & footballs provided. Matching uniforms required.
Playoffs

Tiebreaker Rules

Pool play ties resolved in order:

  1. Win-Loss Record
  2. Head-to-Head Result
  3. Point Differential
  4. Total Points For
  5. Total Points Against
  6. Coin Toss

Bracket play is single elimination.

Official Rules

Flag In The Sand Rulebook

A fast-paced, 5-on-5, non-contact beach flag football event. All play follows standard International Flag guidelines with beach tournament-specific modifications. Tournament Directors and Head Officials have final authority regarding all rule interpretations and game administration.

At A Glance

Core Rules

Format
5-on-5 non-contact beach flag football
Downs
Four downs to score · No first downs
Field
40 yd long × 30 yd wide · Two 5-yd end zones
Drive Start
Every possession begins at the offense's 5-yard line
Halves
(2) 16-min running-clock halves · 2-min halftime
Timeouts
One 60-second timeout per half
Play Clock
25 seconds to snap
QB Pass Clock
5 seconds when there is no legal rush
Rush Line
7 yards behind the line of scrimmage
No Run Zone
Final 5 yards before the goal line — must pass
Contact
No blocking · No intentional contact
Interceptions
Dead immediately · Cannot be returned · 2 points + possession
Footwear
Bare feet or approved sand socks only
Mouthpiece
Required for every player
How It Works

Game Format, Field & Equipment

Game Format

Players on Field
5 per team
Minimum to Start
4 players
Maximum on Field
5 players per team at one time
Substitutions
Unlimited during dead-ball situations
Forfeits
Game time is forfeit time, unless otherwise approved by a FITS Director

Equipment

Provided by Tournament
Official game footballs
Provided by Teams
Matching team jerseys · Legal flag belts
Required
Mouthpiece
Optional
Soft-shell headgear · Gloves · Hats & sunglasses permitted
Flags
Must be securely fastened before every play
Footwear

Tournament officials may prohibit any equipment considered unsafe.

Timing

Game Clock & Start of Game

Game Length
(2) 16-minute running-clock halves · 2-minute halftime
Play Clock
25 seconds to snap after the previous play is ready. Delay of Game is a 5-yard penalty.
Timeouts
One 60-second timeout per team, per half. Unused timeouts do not carry over.
Running Clock
Runs continuously through both halves regardless of score. Stops only for team timeouts, official injury timeouts, and extended officiating or administrative delays.
Coin Toss
Winner chooses Offense, Defense, Direction, or to Defer. The other team receives the choice to begin the second half. Teams switch direction at halftime.
With The Ball

Offensive Rules

Running

  • The quarterback may not run unless the ball has first been legally handed off, pitched, or thrown back.
  • Unlimited handoffs are permitted behind the line of scrimmage.
  • Unlimited laterals and backward passes are permitted, and remain legal anywhere on the field.
  • A forward pass does not have to cross the line of scrimmage.
  • When the football is placed on a player's back, that player must continue to advance the ball and may not hand it back to the quarterback.
  • The football is spotted where it is located when the runner's flag is legally removed.
  • The football must break the plane of the goal line to score.
  • Downfield blocking is prohibited.

No Run Zone

  • The final 5 yards before the goal line is a No Run Zone.
  • When the line of scrimmage is inside the No Run Zone, running plays are prohibited — the offense must score by a forward pass.

Passing

  • The quarterback has 5 seconds to throw the football when there is no legal rush.
  • Once a handoff or backward pitch occurs, the 5-second count ends.
  • If a legal rusher crosses the rush line, the 5-second count no longer applies.
  • There is no "arm in motion" — if the quarterback still has possession when the flag is pulled, the play is ruled a sack.
  • Any part of the passer's body behind the line of scrimmage makes the forward pass legal.

Receiving

  • Every player is eligible to catch a pass.
  • The quarterback becomes an eligible receiver after a legal handoff or backward pitch.
  • Receivers must have at least 1 foot in bounds to complete a catch.
On Defense

Defensive Rules & Ball Status

Rushing the Quarterback

  • Rushers must begin at least 7 yards behind the line of scrimmage. Officials will identify the rush line before each play.
  • Players inside the 7-yard rush line may not enter the backfield before a legal rush.
  • A rusher who establishes a legal lane has the right to that lane. The offense may not intentionally impede a legal rusher.

Pass Coverage

  • Contact with receivers is prohibited. Incidental contact while both players are making a legitimate play on the football is not a foul.
  • Face guarding without significant contact is legal.
  • Defensive pass interference in the end zone places the football at the 1-yard line.
  • Blocking a receiver before the football arrives is offensive pass interference.

Fumbles

  • A fumble is dead immediately. The football is spotted where possession was lost. Loose balls may not be advanced.
  • A snap that contacts the ground is immediately dead.

Lost Flag

If a player's flag unintentionally falls off before or during a play, the player remains live until legally touched with one hand between the shoulders and knees.

Scoring

Point Values

6
Touchdown
1
Extra Pt (3yd)
2
2-Pt (10yd)
2
Interception
2
Safety
Point After
Offensive captain must declare a 1-point (3-yd) or 2-point (10-yd) attempt before the try
Interceptions
Dead immediately and may not be returned under any circumstances. Awards 2 points and the football to the defense at its own 5-yard line.
Safety
2 points. Defensive team begins its next possession at its own 5-yard line.
Overtime

Extra Point Shootout

  1. Article 1. A coin toss determines first possession. Each team receives one 30-second timeout per overtime period.
  2. Article 2. If more than one overtime period is required, teams alternate the order of possession each overtime period.
  3. Article 3. During each overtime period, teams may elect to attempt either a 1-point conversion from the 3-yard line, or a 2-point conversion from the 10-yard line. Teams must go for 2 in the 3rd overtime and beyond.
  4. Article 4. The winner is determined once the value of one team's successful extra point attempt exceeds the opposing team's attempt, after both teams have had an equal opportunity to attempt their conversion.
Penalties

Penalty Enforcement

Unless otherwise specified, penalties are enforced from the previous spot. Because Flag In the Sand does not use first downs, penalties are administered using yardage, replay of down, or loss of down.

Foul Penalty
False Start5 yards, replay the down
Delay of Game5 yards, replay the down
Offside5 yards, replay the down
Encroachment5 yards, replay the down
Illegal Motion5 yards, loss of down
Illegal Shift5 yards, loss of down
Illegal Forward Pass5 yards, loss of down
Illegal Advancement5 yards, loss of down
Flag Guarding5 yards, loss of down
Illegal Blocking5 yards, loss of down
Offensive Pass Interference5 yards, loss of down
Defensive Pass InterferenceSpot foul or 10 yards from the previous spot (offense's choice), replay the down. In the end zone, the ball is placed at the 1-yard line.
Holding (Defense)5 yards from the spot of the foul, replay the down
Holding (Offense)5 yards from the spot of the foul, loss of down
Illegal Contact (Defense)5 yards from the previous spot or spot of the foul, replay the down
Illegal Contact (Offense)5 yards, loss of down
Early Flag Pull5 yards, replay the down
Stripping / Attempted Stripping5 yards from the spot of the foul, replay the down
Roughing the Passer10 yards, replay the down
Personal Foul / Unnecessary Roughness15 yards. Defensive foul: replay the down. Offensive foul: loss of down.
Unsportsmanlike Conduct15 yards. Defensive foul: replay the down. Offensive foul: loss of down.
Charging5 yards from the spot of the foul, loss of down
Impeding the Rusher5 yards, loss of down
Illegal ParticipationOffensive: 5 yards, loss of down. Defensive: 5 yards, replay the down.
Last Man Rule15 yards from the spot of the foul. If the foul occurs inside the opponent's 5-yard line and prevents an apparent touchdown, the referee may award a touchdown.
Conduct

Sportsmanship & Officials

Sportsmanship & Officials' Discretion

Players, coaches, and spectators are expected to demonstrate respect for officials, opponents, teammates, volunteers, and tournament staff. Unsportsmanlike conduct, fighting, taunting, abusive language, or dangerous play may result in penalties, player ejection, or removal from the tournament. Spectators may also be removed from the event for unsportsmanlike behavior.

Tournament officials may assess additional penalties, player disqualification, or ejection for flagrant, repeated, or unsportsmanlike conduct. The Tournament Director and Head Officials reserve the right to make rulings in the interest of player safety, sportsmanship, fair play, and tournament administration. All decisions are final.

Who Can Play

Rosters & Eligibility

Format
Games are 5v5. Teams must have a minimum of 5 players on the roster. Roster maximum is up to each team's discretion.
Official Roster
Only players listed on the official FITS waiver/roster form may play.
Waivers
Players under 18 require a parent/guardian signature. Players 18+ may sign for themselves.
Playing Up/Down
Playing up is allowed. Playing down is not — a team found playing with an ineligible player forfeits all contests and is removed from the tournament with no refund.
Multiple Teams
A player may play on 2 teams, provided the teams are in different divisions.

The Movement

Flag Football's Explosive Growth

Flag football is the fastest-growing sport in America — and it's headed to the Olympics. Here's why now is the time to get on the sand.

By The Numbers

National Growth

2.4M+
Youth Athletes Playing
500K
Girls Ages 6-17 (2023)
63%
Girls Growth Since 2019
68,847
Girls in HS ('24-'25)
60%
1-Year HS Growth
250+
Colleges Offering It
High School & College

Fastest-Growing Emerging Sport

HS Participation
68,847 girls played high school flag football in the 2024-25 school year — up 60% in a single year.
New Programs
Nearly 1,000 additional high schools added girls flag football that same year.
NFHS Recognition
The NFHS has described girls flag football as the nation's fastest-growing emerging high school sport.
State Sanctioning
16 states have officially sanctioned girls flag football, with 2 more expected to sanction it by 2027. 22 additional states have pilot or independent programs.
College Programs
250+ colleges and universities now offer women's flag football — varsity, club, or emerging.
NCAA Championship
The NCAA is working toward a National Collegiate Championship, with the first championship potentially arriving as soon as Spring 2028.
2028 Los Angeles

Going Olympic

Flag football will make its Olympic debut at the 2028 Summer Games in Los Angeles — putting the sport on the world's biggest stage and fueling record participation at every level, from grade school to college.

Who We Are

Bringing the Gridiron to the Coast

Flag In The Sand is built by the same team behind Soccer In The Sand — the gold standard for beach sports since 2006. Over 20 years, we have perfected a coastal tournament model spanning 12 iconic beaches across 9 states.

After two decades of success, we are bringing that same organization and passion to flag football — the fastest-growing youth sport in America, with participation up 30%+ in the last decade and inclusion in the 2028 Olympic Games.

The flags are ready. The sand is waiting.
